newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina mulling YPF-backed bonds - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina mulling YPF-backed bonds - report.

text.p: Argentina is considering issuing bonds backed by shares it still holds in oil firm YPF SA in 1997, local newspapers quoted Economy Minister Roque Fernandez as saying.
"This one of the numerous options the government has for raising international capital next year," Fernandez said in London, according to La Nacion.
The bonds would be convertible to shares in YPF after five years. The government has a 20-percent share in the company, equivalent to about $2 billion.
The government is also talking with an investment bank about financing the final payments still owed by YPF workers for their 10 percent share in the company, local newspapers reported.
Under the terms of YPF's privatization the shares awarded to employees cannot be listed on the stock market until the state has fully paid for them.
Financial daily El Cronista cited Economy Ministry sources as saying the pay-off of the workers' shares would bring the government about $500 million.
